title: Frequently Asked Questions (FAQs)
gist: A subscriber-support FAQ page, not editorial content: Al-Monitor justifies its paywall as the funding mechanism for a 'small but mighty' Middle East newsroom and describes a two-tier product -- 'All-Access' web/app plus archive versus a cheaper email-only 'Daily Briefing' -- with self-service cancellation, no refunds, and coupon-code pricing.

insights.claim: Al-Monitor frames its paywall not as a revenue maximiser but as the mechanism that keeps a small Middle East newsroom editorially independent and financially self-sufficient.
insights.speaker: Al-Monitor
insights.so_what: A reader-revenue-first model at a niche geopolitical publisher signals durable subscription pricing power in specialist news -- relevant to the wider unbundling of general-interest media.
insights.quote: The paywall helps ensure our award-winning content remains strong and self-sufficient.
insights.locator: Why do you have a paywall?

insights.claim: The publisher's stated demand argument is that independent and fair Middle East coverage is 'more necessary than ever', i.e. it is selling into rising geopolitical uncertainty rather than into a stable news cycle.
insights.speaker: Al-Monitor
insights.so_what: Specialist geopolitical media revenue is levered to regional conflict intensity -- a countercyclical subscription business worth noting alongside defence and risk-consulting exposure.
insights.quote: Independent and fair coverage of the Middle East is more necessary than ever these days.
insights.locator: Why do you have a paywall?

insights.claim: Al-Monitor segments its product into 'All-Access' -- unlimited web and app access to 24/7 news and analysis, interviews, newsletters, the full archive, webinars and select live events -- and a cheaper email-only 'Daily Briefing' tier.
insights.speaker: Al-Monitor
insights.so_what: Classic good-better ladder with the archive and events reserved for the top tier: the archive is the retention moat, the email tier is the low-friction acquisition funnel.
insights.locator: What is included in my subscription?

insights.claim: The Daily Briefing email tier is explicitly walled off from web and app content, so the cheaper tier cannot cannibalise the flagship subscription.
insights.speaker: Al-Monitor
insights.so_what: Deliberate downgrade-blocking is how subscription publishers protect ARPU -- look for the same design when assessing any media company's tiering.
insights.quote: this subscription tier does not offer all-access to the web and app content
insights.locator: What is included in my subscription?

insights.claim: Promotional pricing is handled through a 'coupon code' field applied at the point of subscribing, indicating discount-led acquisition is a standing part of the funnel rather than an exception.
insights.speaker: Al-Monitor
insights.so_what: Heavy reliance on promo codes usually means reported subscriber growth carries discount-driven churn risk at first renewal.
insights.locator: I have a promotional code. How do I apply it?

insights.claim: Cancellation is permitted at any time but no refunds are issued on subscriptions already purchased, so revenue is recognised through the paid term regardless of when a subscriber quits.
insights.speaker: Al-Monitor
insights.so_what: No-refund terms smooth reported revenue but push dissatisfaction into non-renewal -- churn shows up a full billing cycle late in the numbers.
insights.quote: We cannot issue refunds for subscriptions already purchased.
insights.locator: What is your cancellation and refund policy?

insights.claim: Al-Monitor routes all cancellations through a self-service 'Manage My Subscription' flow and states twice that its customer service team does not process cancellations, deliberately removing the human save-desk from the churn path.
insights.speaker: Al-Monitor
insights.so_what: Self-service-only cancellation is both a cost saver and a regulatory exposure under click-to-cancel rules -- a recurring compliance item for subscription businesses.
insights.quote: Please note, our Customer service team does not process cancellations.
insights.locator: How do I reach customer service?
